To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) standard methods already reach an accuracy level of about 95% on the MALDI-TOF dataset, (ii) using the hierarchical structure does not consistently help, and (iii) the most important information in the dataset comes from the MALDI-MS spectra, not from the hierarchical structure.

1) standard methods are very efficient in microbial identification; 2) structured methods do not systematically perform better than standard methods; 3) standard methods are able to discriminate between closely-related species, a case where the use of the hierarchical structure is not helpful; 4) structured methods can be useful to identify species that are more distant in the hierarchical structure.

(1) structured methods are not consistently better than flat methods for microbial identification, and (2) the hierarchical structure of the species is a source of confusion in the learning process, which may explain why structured methods perform poorly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving microbial identification systems, and we propose a benchmark that could be used to evaluate the performance of new methods.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
structured machine learning methods are promising for microbial identification, but that more data are necessary to confirm this.
structured methods are more appropriate when the hierarchy is not too deep, and that they are not always better than standard ones.
structured methods should be preferred when they are expected to perform significantly better than the best performing standard method.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of structured machine learning techniques for microbial identification is still an open issue.
, although the use of the underlying structure is not always useful, it does not harm and could be helpful for future work.
, for this particular dataset and for the considered methods, the hierarchical information is not helpful.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the specific case of MALDI-TOF identification, the use of a priori information about the underlying hierarchical structure does not improve the accuracy of the methods, but that it is still a valuable tool to gain a better understanding of the underlying mechanisms.
, although the hierarchical structure of the data is known, the performance of structured methods is not consistently better than standard methods.
, in order to benefit from structured learning methods, it is crucial to have an appropriate dataset.
